title: Luteinizing hormone (LH)

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: This test measures the level of luteinizing hormone (LH), which is made by the pituitary gland at the base of the brain. LH plays a role in sexual development in children and in fertility in adults.
context: What a result means depends on your sex and age. In people who menstruate, LH changes through the monthly cycle, so testing may be done at a set time; in people age 45 or older, higher LH is often a normal sign of perimenopause and menopause.
aboveRange: In people who menstruate, a higher level may be associated with the ovaries not working as usual, such as with PCOS or primary ovarian insufficiency, or with approaching menopause
In men, a higher level may be associated with a condition affecting the testicles
belowRange: A lower level is often associated with a condition of the pituitary gland or hypothalamus
In people who menstruate, a lower level with missed periods may also be linked to extreme exercise, poor nutrition, stress, or being very underweight
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
